objective: Audit the finite affine-graph trichotomy, repair the proposed one-switch normal form, construct exact mixed-SCC formal survivors, and test whether existing H72 models satisfy the finite-state hypotheses.

quantifiers: every finite directed multigraph whose nonempty edge labels are shortcut parity blocks, for the symbolic theorems P107 through P111
every deterministic partial two-label graph on one through three vertices, for the E30 exhaustive audit
the 512-block exact mixed one-state schedule recorded in E30
the mandatory adversarial families and the preserved obstructions NG02, NG17, NG19, and NG21 through NG29
the Phase 7, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, and 17 finite abstractions named in the applicability audit
exact_scope.completeness: P107 through P111 and NG30 are symbolic exact claims under their written finite-graph hypotheses. E30 is exhaustive only for the recorded graph class, path depth, schedule length, and project files.

arithmetic.floating_point_role: none in acceptance; logarithmic discrepancy appears only as notation and every decision compares integer powers of two and three

verifier_reconstructs: edge affine constants using an explicit odd-position sum
SCCs and simple-cycle signs with a different graph traversal
all deterministic partial graphs in a different enumeration order
the mixed schedule and beta identity from literal affine composition
the four-stage NG30 counterfamily and project-model digests

stop_conditions: Reject any graph classification whose cycle signs are decided by floating point.
Retract the proposed single-switch normal form at the first exact alternating-sign SCC-chain counterexample.
Do not classify a project abstraction as an exact finite automaton unless its transition state is closed and prefix-complete.
Do not promote a coherent 2-adic source to a positive ordinary integer.
Enter the proof-claim emergency protocol before changing proves_collatz.
interpretation_boundary: The finite-state trichotomy is a theorem about a supplied closed finite graph, not a proof that the H72 language has such a graph.
A mixed SCC supplies formal balanced paths but does not supply a positive ordinary Collatz source.
The EXT07 exclusion applies to the constructed balanced itinerary, not every path through a mixed SCC.
Finite graph enumeration and source-lift samples have no asymptotic ordinary-integrality implication.
H72 and the Collatz conjecture remain open; proves_collatz remains false.
